interpretation.allocator: Allocation/reallocation/bytes/region-peak counters are separate observations; failed allocation calls are zero and no allocator adoption gate is applied.
interpretation.controls: All individual >1.05 pair flags are retained below; control p99 tail flags remain review evidence and prevent treating the primary result as a universal latency claim.
interpretation.primary_latency_evidence: Primary native p50 whole-child paired median and bootstrap CI satisfy the frozen gate.
interpretation.rss: GNU time process-lifetime high-water RSS is reported descriptively; it is not an adoption gate and no causal RSS mechanism is inferred.
interpretation.scope: Four fixed corpus cases, warm filesystem mode, CPU affinity 12 without exclusive-host or physical-cold-cache guarantees, release binaries, fresh sequential children; no general workload claim.

allocator_adoption.reason: allocator counters are separate observations; no automatic adoption gate

allocator_reduction_crosscheck.reallocation_calls: independently recomputed from raw allocator reports; inherited reduction schema does not include this field

guard_regression_review.basis: all 72 child reports, producer sidecars, fixed corpus identities, sample alignment, semantic scan evidence, allocator vectors, zero-failure vectors, and source-version/route fences were independently replayed; root verification also passes
guard_regression_review.uncertainty: fixed corpus and quality receipts do not establish universal correctness or exclusive-host performance behavior; control p99 flags remain visible and adoption interpretation is scoped to the primary gate

replayed.statistics: recomputed from each retained sorted raw elapsed vector using floored midpoint p50 and nearest-rank p95/p99; no sample pooling; RSS ratios use retained GNU /usr/bin/time peak-rss-kib.txt

uncertainty: Control p99 flags are retained as observed whole-child tail variation; this replay cannot attribute mechanism or establish universal/exclusive-host behavior.
The capture and source semantics do not by themselves establish correctness outside the sealed fixed corpus and quality receipts.
